<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33ab543913125b53feec6c116f13d616261a908c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8d55baa7fa4691bddd790997d1b4e644edc4f438` — the merge of head `fd9a0e600dc5cd9c3cdcf15e71b1b29d205da9ba` into base `33ab543913125b53feec6c116f13d616261a908c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8d55baa7fa4691bddd790997d1b4e644edc4f438 && git checkout 8d55baa7fa4691bddd790997d1b4e644edc4f438
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33ab543913125b53feec6c116f13d616261a908c fd9a0e600dc5cd9c3cdcf15e71b1b29d205da9ba && git checkout -B drift-repro 33ab543913125b53feec6c116f13d616261a908c && git merge --no-ff fd9a0e600dc5cd9c3cdcf15e71b1b29d205da9ba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33ab543913125b53feec6c116f13d616261a908c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33ab543913125b53feec6c116f13d616261a908c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fd9a0e600dc5cd9c3cdcf15e71b1b29d205da9ba`

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #27334 (body and all six comments, including triage 6484963623, the retriage 6495077738, its answer 6496297039, the release 6500886024, the claim 6501842999 and the os-dev-report 6503460374), PR #27674 (body, five-file list, net diff against `main` from the files endpoint), the 53 check-runs on `fd9a0e60`, and the cited code on the head and on `origin/main` (`idp-locale-claim.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`, `index.ts`, `implicit-account-linking.ts`, `package.json`).

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`AuthManager.applyIdpLocaleClaim(userId, claim)` — new public method on an already-exported class** (`auth-manager.ts:2183`). Public surface of the published `@objectstack/plugin-auth` entry grows by one method. **Right.** It is a thin wrapper that returns `this.idpLocale.apply(userId, claim)` on the manager's own `IdpLocaleSync` instance, so no second instance, no second engine, locale list or auth store; this is exactly the shape ruling 6496297039 allows ("export the existing `IdpLocaleSync` path (or a thin wrapper over it), and do not copy it"). The card's own two shapes (`IdpLocaleSync` plus deps type, or a free `applyIdpLocale({ engine, userId, claim, supported })`) would each have let a caller build a second instance with its own deps; the chosen shape is the one that keeps one owner and is reachable from outside the package through the kernel service `auth` (`auth-plugin.ts:776`).
2. **`export type { IdpLocaleClaim }` — new type-only export from the entry** (`index.ts:42`). **Right.** It is the argument type of the method, `{ providerId?, value: unknown }`, carries no runtime code, and the `#25224` header rule of `index.ts` is honoured: no new module-level name of `auth-manager.ts` was added to the by-name list; the method rides on `AuthManager`, which was already listed.
3. **`IdpLocaleSync.apply(userId, claim, ctx?)` — new public method on an UNEXPORTED class.** Not a published-surface change. Compared base `settle` on `origin/main` with head `apply`: the `try` block is moved verbatim (supported-locale guard with the once-only warn, `getEngine()`, `authContextOf(ctx) ?? resolveAuth()`, the `sys_user` read, the `idp-locale:` record read, `decideIdpLocaleWrite`, the column write, `replaceIdpLocaleRecord`, the never-throw `warn`). `settle` keeps its own guards and now ends in `await this.apply(userId, claim, ctx)`. The rule and the record identifier `idp-locale:USERID` are unchanged. **Right.**
4. **Accept set of the new call.** The only added logic is the guard `if (typeof userId !== 'string' || !userId || !claim) return;` before the `try`. A JavaScript caller passing a bad id or no claim gets a resolved promise and no write; a refusing store gets one `warn`. The call never throws, as every docblock says. The no-context path is sound: `authContextOf(undefined)` returns `undefined` (`implicit-account-linking.ts:218`), so the auth store comes from `resolveAuth()` = the manager's `linkingContext()`, the same fallback the OIDC path uses when its endpoint context carries no auth. **Right.**
5. **Pure helpers (`readIdpLocaleClaim`, `resolveIdpLocale`, `decideIdpLocaleWrite`, `idpLocaleRecordIdentifier`) and the class `IdpLocaleSync` stay unexported.** **Right** under the one-owner ruling: publishing the steps would let a caller rebuild the rule beside it. `readIdpLocaleClaim` reads a better-auth `validateUserInfo` source shape the sso-exchange door does not hold.
6. **OIDC path's observable behaviour unchanged.** The existing end-of-chain OIDC cases in `idp-locale-claim.test.ts` are untouched; a new spy pins that a real platform-IdP sign-in settles through `IdpLocaleSync.apply` once, with the user id, `{ providerId, value: 'zh-CN' }` and the endpoint context. **Right.**
7. **Card "Done when".** `import { AuthManager, type IdpLocaleClaim } from '@objectstack/plugin-auth'` gives a caller outside the package the same write-or-keep decision and the same `idp-locale:` record the OIDC JIT path uses; the three rule cases (unset: written with record; still the recorded value: overwritten, column and record; local choice: kept, `engine.update` never called, `sys_verification` rows byte-identical) run from the entry module. The test imports `./index`, the module tsup builds as the entry, rather than the package name; the reason given (a self-alias in `vitest.config.ts` is outside the declared surface) holds and `./index` is the same module. **Accepted.**
8. **Not on `IAuthService` in `packages/spec`.** The method is on the concrete `AuthManager`, so a host typing the `auth` service as `IAuthService` casts to `AuthManager`, as this package's own tests do. `packages/spec` is outside the declared surface (ruling 6496297039: "the `plugin-auth` entry export and its test, with no other file under `packages/plugins`"), and adding it to the contract would have made this a schema-face PR. **Right as scoped**; see ③.

Gate verdicts, read off the check-runs on `fd9a0e60`: every non-skipped run concluded `success` — Test Core (shards 1 to 8 and the aggregate), TypeScript Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint & Repo Gates (ESLint, repo and tooling gates, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, CI/release/engine gates, scoped query-options erasure, scoped slot lookup and corpus, scoped tooling self-tests), Build Core, Check Changeset (twice), PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label. The skipped runs are the opt-in harnesses, the UI matrix shards, Live E2E, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance and the schedule gate: none is owed by a diff confined to `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src` plus a changeset. The Docs Drift comment is advisory; its three hand-written pages name `AuthManager` only in passing (`auth-service.mdx:56`, `services-checklist.mdx:298`, `authentication.mdx:60,427`), none enumerates its methods, so no page is falsified and no docs edit is owed; the releases page is read-only by rule.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27334-idp-locale-rule-export.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch`, with the two line-initial declarations `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, a migration-free body ("Nothing to do for existing hosts"). The PR body carries the same two lines.
- **`patch` is right, the order's `minor` is not.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, verbatim: "The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least **`minor`** on a package the diff moves, `none` takes **`patch`**; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". The diff adds no key, value or metadata type an author can write, so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch`. CLAUDE.md names AGENTS.md the single source of truth, so where the card's Work step 2 and the dispatch order said "minor", AGENTS.md governs. The `Check Changeset` check-run on the head concluded `success`, which is the gate's own reading of the same two lines.
- **Clause-②:** `yes (widening)`. Right: the diff enlarges the published entry's public surface (one method on an exported class, one type export) and removes or tightens nothing, so the `(widening)` arm is the only arm; no `(narrowing)`, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition owed. No published schema (`packages/spec` untouched, no api-surface ledger moves) and no governed path in the five files, so the face is the declaration alone and the record's Served-tier is `TIER_DEFAULT`.
- `skip-changeset` would be wrong here and was not used; the package is published (`"@objectstack/plugin-auth"` 18.2.0, not private, `exports["."]` is `dist/index.*`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0] — "The order names a minor changeset; AGENTS.md grades Metadata-protocol none as patch. Which stands?"** Answered: **A, `patch` stands**, as shipped. The grading rule is quoted in ② and admits no reading under which a `Metadata-protocol: none` change takes `minor`; the dispatch order and the card's "minor" were written before the level-by-kind rule was applied to this diff. Nothing to escalate.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0] — `applyIdpLocaleClaim` is on `AuthManager`, not on `IAuthService` (`packages/spec`).** Accepted as out of scope: the declared surface excludes `packages/spec`, and the consumer named in the PR (objectstack-ai/cloud#3159) reaches the running manager through `ctx.getService('auth')` and casts, as this package's tests do. If the cloud half wants the call on the contract type, that is a new card on the schema face, not a rider here. Not a must-fix.
- **out_of_scope_findings[1] — three stray empty files written to `/` in the dev's container.** Nothing in the repo; the diff's five files are the whole change. No action.
- **Dev flag — the entry test imports `./index`, not `@objectstack/plugin-auth`.** Accepted, see ① item 7.
- **Dev flag — `Skills-docs: none`.** Consistent with the diff: no file under `skills/**` is touched and the change introduces no metadata key or value a skill would teach.
- **Dev flag — generated ledgers: none to regenerate.** Consistent: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` keeps no api-surface snapshot, and the check-runs that read export ledgers (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`) are green on the head.
- **Dev flag — `premise_still_valid: true`.** Confirmed on the head's parent side: `origin/main` `index.ts` names nothing from `idp-locale-claim.ts`.
- **Docs Drift advisory.** No edit owed (① gate paragraph); the release-owned page stays untouched.

Must-fix: none.
